products.variable: Field-measured depth to water below land surface in a well, parameter 72019.
products.units: Feet below local land-surface datum. Check parameter, reference, units and measuring-point adjustments for each well.
products.data_nature: Discrete groundwater-level observations made during well visits
products.spatial_support: Individual monitoring well and screened aquifer interval. Nearby wells may represent different aquifers.
products.temporal_support: Irregular individual visits with time, quality/approval and well condition qualifiers.
products.temporal_coverage: Period of record varies by well. The checked example is a 1969 field measurement. There is no assumed shared start or sampling frequency.
products.geographic_coverage: U.S. monitoring wells, including participating territories where records exist. Well and aquifer coverage is site-specific.
supported_use_cases: Assess groundwater-level anomalies or drawdown by well after checking depth reference, pumping conditions and measurement history.
non_uses: Aquifer storage volume, river stage or hydraulic head above an absolute geodetic datum.
limitations: Depth below local land surface cannot be subtracted across wells to infer a hydraulic gradient without surveyed elevations and consistent datums.
Sparse visits, pumping and changes to the measuring point can obscure seasonal trends.
products.dependence_notes: Networks include USGS and partner agencies. Check agency and well identifiers before treating records from other portals as independent.
products.access_method: Filter field measurements to parameter 72019, a monitoring location or bounding box, and project dates. Follow pagination and retain depth reference, approval and qualifiers.
products.license_notes: Credit USGS and the measuring agency. Check third-party notices and preserve station, parameter, datum and qualifier information.
unresolved_questions: Project-specific sampling, quality flags and valid spatial coverage need checking in the selected provider files.
products.vertical_reference: Depth below local land-surface datum. A separate surveyed land elevation and its vertical datum are required to compute comparable groundwater elevations.
